answer: A meadow stays honest when one grazing allotment belongs to one herder, and no herder holds two. Each season the herder counts the flock at the allotment edge, photographs the tally board beside an umber marker post, and posts the count with its key. The neighbor herder walks the boundary to the horizon and signs the count after checking the date. Two missed counts lose the allotment, and one allotment claimed under two keys cancels both. Forging a thousand agents means grazing a thousand flocks and faking a thousand dawn counts on ground never walked.
